decisions.reason: The candidate already has a complete same-message MODIFY recording the sensor-board power and signal input connector types and pinouts; no additional update or removal is required.
The candidate already has a same-message INTRODUCE that fully records the SPS30 connector type, cable compatibility, supply, I2C signals, SEL connection, and ground connection.
The sensor-board connector inventory does not change the standalone USB supply source, regulator, activation condition, rail coverage, or unresolved regulator-capacity question.
The sensor-board connector specification does not discuss or change the charge-status LED chain or external charge-LED interface.
Identifying SPS30 as a 5V-connected sensor is consistent with the existing powered-load state and does not change the boost converter, enable GPIO, switching policy, or load inventory.
The six-pin signal connector described at message 371 is the main-to-sensor-board interface and does not replace or modify the separate J_PWR_SIGNAL USB D+/D- route.
The connector fanout is compatible with the existing 3.3V downstream-load description and does not change DCDC1 voltage, current rating, or regulation role.
The source specifies sensor-board connector topology but does not change the power-board BOM, component sourcing, or assembly-readiness obligations.
Routing SDA0/SCL0 and SDA1/SCL1 through sensor connectors does not change the established pull-up placement, resistance, bus speed, cable assumptions, or optional series-resistor policy.
The source confirms power and signal connectivity to the sensor board but does not change the monitored rails, INA3221 selection, monitor placement, measurement coverage, or spare channel count.
The JST-PH connector in the source is a four-pin sensor-board power input, not the separate three-pin battery connector, so the battery interface remains unchanged.
The source enumerates sensor-board module connectors and does not change the main-board panel button, switch, reset, touch, or BOOT-button interfaces.
